the temporal placement of water in an interval schedule modulates the pattern of lever-pressing but not water consumption.

(1) schedule-induced drinking is not ubiquitous, and (2) the amount of water consumed during a drinking opportunity is a decreasing function of the time from the next food reinforcer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a drinking opportunity on a fixed-intensity schedule of reinforcement.
the effects of a "probe stimulus" on behavior maintained by a fixed-interval (FI) 1-min schedule of food presentation.
the effects of the temporal placement of drinking opportunities within a fixed-interval reinforcement cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of the drinking opportunity on lever pressing were due primarily to its temporal placement within the fixed-interval cycle.
the drinking behavior of a rat is a function of its current physiological status and the environmental contingencies of reinforcement.
the temporal placement of the drinking opportunity in the reinforcement cycle is a critical determinant of the amount of drinking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal placement of an opportunity to drink is a critical factor in the occurrence of schedule-induced drinking.
ubiquitousness" is a function of the temporal proximity of the drinking opportunity to a reinforcement.
the "ubiquity" of drinking induced by a stimulus is a function of the temporal placement of the stimulus and the nature of the stimulus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal placement of an opportunity to drink in the reinforcement cycle is a crucial variable in determining the magnitude of schedule-induced drinking.
it is not enough to say that drinking is induced by a schedule.

schedule-induced drinking, as well as the other schedule-induced behaviors, are not ubiquitous and are not a function of the schedule alone but are a function of both the schedule and the intruding stimulus.
